mainTopic: The word מִשְׁרַת: טעם כעיקר (רבנן) vs. היתר מצטרף לאיסור (רבי עקיבא, followed by רבי יוחנן), and where each side learns טעם כעיקר from
overview: This amud continues a challenge against רבי יוחנן, who learns from the word מִשְׁרַת (the נזיר may not drink anything 'soaked' from grapes) that permitted food joins with forbidden food to make up the forbidden amount (היתר מצטרף לאיסור). A ברייתא uses the same word for טעם כעיקר, the rule that the taste of a forbidden food counts like the food itself. It then spreads that rule to כלאים, ערלה and the whole Torah with a קל וחומר. The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows the רבנן, while רבי יוחנן follows רבי עקיבא, and it shows from a ברייתא that רבי עקיבא holds היתר מצטרף לאיסור. Next the גמרא asks where רבי עקיבא learns טעם כעיקר. It first suggests בשר בחלב, but that is a חידוש, so it switches to גיעולי גוים, the koshering of non-Jewish pots. The רבנן say גיעולי גוים is also a חידוש, because even a same-day pot gives a slightly spoiled taste. Finally, רב אחא בריה דרב אויא argues that if the רבנן spread their lesson from מִשְׁרַת to the whole Torah, רבי עקיבא's lesson should spread too. רב אשי's answer begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The word 'soaked' teaches that taste counts like substance
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the word מִשְׁרַת teaches טעם כעיקר. A נזיר who drinks water that tastes like wine from soaked grapes is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'soaked' comes to teach that the taste of a forbidden food counts like the food itself. So if someone soaked grapes in water, and the water has the taste of wine, a נזיר who drinks it is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the end of a ברייתא to challenge רבי יוחנן. The ברייתא uses the word מִשְׁרַת for טעם כעיקר, which is not the lesson רבי יוחנן takes from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן learned from מִשְׁרַת that a permitted food joins a forbidden food to make up the forbidden amount (היתר מצטרף לאיסור). This ברייתא says the word teaches a different rule: forbidden taste alone makes a food forbidden. If the word is already used up for טעם כעיקר, how can רבי יוחנן learn his rule from it?

keyTerms.meaning: The taste of a forbidden food has the same status as the food itself
'Soaked' - the word in the פסוק about what a נזיר may not drink
He soaked
Liable (to punishment)

steps.confusionAlert: Here the water has no actual grape pieces in it, only the taste of wine. That is exactly the point: the taste by itself is enough to make the נזיר liable.

phrases.english: To establish that taste is like the substance.
phrases.notes: Continues a ברייתא explaining the word מִשְׁרַת.

phrases.english: For if one soaked grapes in water,
and it has the taste of wine, he (the נזיר) is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that was quoted, on the previous amud, as a challenge to רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's use of מִשְׁרַת to teach היתר מצטרף לאיסור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word מִשְׁרַת is already used to teach טעם כעיקר, so it cannot also be the source for רבי יוחנן's rule.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from נזיר to כלאים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא argues that if the milder איסור of נזיר has טעם כעיקר, then the stricter איסור of כלאים must have it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here you learn the rule for the whole Torah. A נזיר's איסור is not forever, it is not an איסור הנאה, and it can be undone. Yet the Torah made taste count like the food itself for him. כלאים is forbidden forever, is an איסור הנאה, and cannot be undone. Isn't it logical that its taste should count like the food itself?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא takes the טעם כעיקר rule from נזיר and spreads it to כלאים using a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נזיר is weaker than כלאים in three ways: it is not forever, it forbids only eating and not benefit, and a חכם can release the נדר. If even the weaker case has טעם כעיקר, the stronger case of כלאים surely does. This turns a rule about one person into a general rule for all of Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: A permanent prohibition
A prohibition against getting any benefit, not only eating
A way to undo the prohibition (for a נזיר, release by a חכם)
Forbidden mixtures; here, grain or vegetables grown in a vineyard
'And if...' - the opening word of a קל וחומר

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for treating טעם כעיקר as a rule that applies across the whole Torah, not just to נזיר.

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן אַתָּה דָּן לְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ:
phrases.english: From here you derive the rule for the entire Torah:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה נָזִיר שֶׁאֵין אִיסּוּרוֹ אִיסּוּר עוֹלָם,
phrases.english: Just as a nazirite, whose prohibition is not a permanent prohibition,
and whose prohibition is not a prohibition on benefit,
and whose prohibition can be undone,
yet the Torah made taste like the substance for him,
then diverse kinds, whose prohibition is permanent,
and whose prohibition is a prohibition on benefit,
and whose prohibition cannot be undone,
is it not logical that the Torah should make taste like the substance?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן אַתָּה דָּן לְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the טעם כעיקר rule for נזיר from step 1 and extends it with a קל וחומר.
steps.raayaObject: That טעם כעיקר applies to כלאים and to the whole Torah
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the milder איסור of נזיר

steps.title: ערלה follows too, being stricter in two ways
steps.stepSummary: The same reasoning applies to ערלה, which is stricter than נזיר in two of the three ways. This completes the challenge to רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same is true of ערלה, which is stricter in two of the ways!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds ערלה to the קל וחומר. With that, the challenge against רבי יוחנן is complete, and the גמרא is setting up for an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערלה is not forbidden forever, since the tree's fruit becomes permitted after three years. But it is an איסור הנאה, and the fruit of those first years can never be permitted. Being stricter than נזיר in two ways is enough for the קל וחומר, so טעם כעיקר applies to ערלה as well.

keyTerms.meaning: And the same law applies
Fruit from a tree's first three years, which is forbidden
In two (of the three points of strictness)

phrases.english: And the same is true of orla, on two counts!
phrases.notes: ערלה is an איסור הנאה and cannot be undone, but it is not permanent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the קל וחומר of step 2 to another איסור.
steps.raayaObject: That טעם כעיקר applies to ערלה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The same קל וחומר from נזיר, based on two points of strictness

steps.title: The ברייתא follows the רבנן; רבי יוחנן follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא reflects the view of the רבנן, while רבי יוחנן holds like רבי עקיבא, who reads מִשְׁרַת as teaching היתר מצטרף לאיסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this ברייתא? It is the רבנן. And רבי יוחנן, who said his rule, holds like רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says this ברייתא is one side of a מחלוקת, and רבי יוחנן simply follows the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן use the word מִשְׁרַת for טעם כעיקר. רבי עקיבא uses the same word for היתר מצטרף לאיסור, and רבי יוחנן agrees with רבי עקיבא. So the ברייתא is no problem for רבי יוחנן. This raises the question of where רבי עקיבא learns טעם כעיקר from, which steps 9-16 answer.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whose view is this?' - a way of answering by naming the author of a source
The Sages (the majority view)
A permitted food joins with a forbidden food to make up the forbidden amount

steps.whatToRemember: The word מִשְׁרַת is the subject of a מחלוקת. The רבנן learn טעם כעיקר from it, and רבי עקיבא (followed by רבי יוחנן) learns היתר מצטרף לאיסור from it.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רבי יוחנן rejects טעם כעיקר. It is only saying he does not learn it from this word, because he uses the word for a different rule.

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is the Rabbis,
and Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said his rule, holds like Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised by the ברייתא in steps 1-3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to one side of a מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's reading of מִשְׁרַת as טעם כעיקר seemed binding on everyone, which would contradict רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows the רבנן. רבי יוחנן follows רבי עקיבא, who uses מִשְׁרַת for היתר מצטרף לאיסור.

steps.title: Which statement of רבי עקיבא? A first suggestion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי עקיבא's view is found and suggests a משנה about a נזיר who soaked his bread in wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which רבי עקיבא do we mean? If you say it is the רבי עקיבא of the משנה, as we learned: רבי עקיבא says, a נזיר who soaked his bread in wine, and there is enough in it to join together to make an olive-size, is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to find the source for the רבי עקיבא it just mentioned. It suggests a משנה, and this sets up the next step, which will test whether this משנה really proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4 the גמרא said רבי עקיבא holds היתר מצטרף לאיסור, meaning the permitted food joins with the forbidden food. Now it needs a text where רבי עקיבא actually says this. The משנה looks promising because it talks about bread and wine 'joining' to make an olive-size.

keyTerms.meaning: Which?
If you say (introduces a suggestion that will likely be rejected)
Soaked
To join together
An olive-size, the minimum amount for liability

phrases.english: Which Rabbi Akiva?
phrases.notes: Which statement of רבי עקיבא are we relying on?

phrases.english: If you say the Rabbi Akiva of the Mishnah,
as we learned: Rabbi Akiva says:
a nazir who soaked his bread in wine,
and there is enough in it to join into an olive-size —
he is liable,

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא? אִילֵימָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּמַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the textual source of the רבי עקיבא view used in the תירוץ of Step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which statement of רבי עקיבא shows that he holds היתר מצטרף לאיסור?

steps.title: The משנה may mean wine alone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: maybe the משנה means there is an olive-size of wine by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that it means an olive-size from the bread and the wine together? Maybe it means an olive-size from the wine alone?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggested משנה. It says the משנה could mean that the wine alone adds up to an olive-size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To prove היתר מצטרף לאיסור, we need the bread (permitted) to count toward the olive-size. If the משנה means the soaked wine alone is an olive-size, the bread plays no role, so there is no proof.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
Perhaps
By itself, alone

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it means from the bread and the wine together?
Perhaps it means from the wine alone?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי דְּמִפַּת וּמִיַּיִן? דִּילְמָא מִיַּיִן לְחוֹדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the משנה suggested in Step 5 as a proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the משנה as proof; it does not reject that רבי עקיבא holds היתר מצטרף לאיסור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's wording can be read as an olive-size of wine alone, so it does not show the bread joining in.

steps.title: Why the משנה would still teach something new
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers a possible objection: even if the wine alone is an olive-size, the משנה teaches that a mixture still makes him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: if it means wine alone, what is the point of saying it? It teaches us that he is liable even though the wine is mixed in with something else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks an attack on its rejection. Someone might say the 'wine alone' reading makes the משנה pointless, so the גמרא shows it still teaches a real lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An olive-size of plain wine obviously makes a נזיר liable, so why would the משנה need to say it? The answer is that the wine here is soaked into bread, and the משנה teaches that being part of a mixture does not cancel liability. So the 'wine alone' reading works, and the משנה still cannot prove היתר מצטרף.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces an expected objection)
What is the point of saying it? (it seems obvious)
This is what it teaches us
A mixture

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not bring back the משנה as a proof. It strengthens the rejection by showing that the 'wine alone' reading makes good sense.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: מִיַּיִן לְחוֹדֵיהּ מַאי לְמֵימְרָא?
phrases.english: And if you say: if from the wine alone, what is the point of stating it?
This is what it teaches us:
that even though it is in a mixture, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: מִיַּיִן לְחוֹדֵיהּ מַאי לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the rejection in Step 6 against the objection that the 'wine alone' reading leaves the משנה with nothing to teach.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Completes the rejection of the משנה as a source.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה has a good lesson even when read as wine alone: liability applies even in a mixture.

steps.title: The source is רבי עקיבא in a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי עקיבא clearly says the olive-size is made from bread and wine together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is the רבי עקיבא of the ברייתא, as it was taught: רבי עקיבא says, a נזיר who soaked his bread in wine and ate an olive-size from the bread and the wine is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real source: a ברייתא where רבי עקיבא's words are clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי עקיבא says the olive-size comes 'from the bread and from the wine'. That means the permitted bread counts toward the forbidden amount. This is exactly היתר מצטרף לאיסור, so it supports the answer from Step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (replaces a rejected idea)
As it was taught in a ברייתא
Permitted food joins with forbidden food to make up the amount

steps.whatToRemember: The source for רבי עקיבא's view that היתר מצטרף לאיסור is the ברייתא, not the משנה. Only the ברייתא clearly says the olive-size comes from bread and wine together.

phrases.english: Rather, it is the Rabbi Akiva of the Baraisa.
As it was taught: Rabbi Akiva says:
a nazir who soaked his bread in wine,
and ate an olive-size from the bread and the wine —
he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected משנה with a ברייתא that clearly supports the point.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא where רבי עקיבא rules that an olive-size made of bread and wine together makes the נזיר liable.

steps.title: Where does רבי עקיבא learn taste is like substance?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי עקיבא uses מִשְׁרַת for היתר מצטרף, the גמרא asks where he learns טעם כעיקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא, where does he learn טעם כעיקר from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. It sets up the next step, which gives רבי עקיבא's source for טעם כעיקר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן learned טעם כעיקר from the word מִשְׁרַת. רבי עקיבא uses that same word for היתר מצטרף לאיסור, so it is no longer available to him. If he still holds טעם כעיקר, he needs a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: The taste of a forbidden food counts like the food itself
From where does he learn it?

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא טַעַם כְּעִיקָּר מְנָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva, from where does he learn that taste is like the substance?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא טַעַם כְּעִיקָּר מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting מִשְׁרַת aside for היתר מצטרף, asks for רבי עקיבא's separate source for טעם כעיקר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is רבי עקיבא's source for טעם כעיקר, given that he uses מִשְׁרַת for another lesson?

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns it from בשר בחלב
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב, where only the taste of the milk is in the meat and it is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from meat cooked in milk: isn't it just a taste, and still it is forbidden? Here too, it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא learns טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When meat is cooked in milk, the meat only takes in the taste of the milk, yet the Torah forbids it. That shows taste alone can make food forbidden. רבי עקיבא applies the same rule to other איסורים.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns it (derives it)
Meat cooked in milk
Merely, just
It is no different

steps.whatToRemember: At this stage, רבי עקיבא's source for טעם כעיקר is בשר בחלב, and the רבנן learn טעם כעיקר from מִשְׁרַת itself. The גמרא later drops בשר בחלב as רבי עקיבא's source (step 15) and replaces it with גיעולי גוים (step 16).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי עקיבא also holds טעם כעיקר. The two sides differ only on which verse teaches which rule, and that is why רבי יוחנן can follow רבי עקיבא without trouble from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: He learns it from meat in milk:
Isn't it merely a taste, and yet it is forbidden?
Here too, it is no different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9 by giving בשר בחלב as רבי עקיבא's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From בשר בחלב: there only the milk's taste is in the meat, yet it is forbidden, so taste counts like the substance.

steps.title: The רבנן do not learn from בשר בחלב because it is a חידוש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן don't learn טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב, and answers that בשר בחלב is a חידוש, so we cannot learn other laws from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, why don't they learn from this? We do not learn from בשר בחלב, because it is a חידוש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the רבנן and asks why they don't learn טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב like רבי עקיבא does. The answer is that בשר בחלב is a חידוש, so nothing can be learned from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חידוש is a law that goes against normal logic or normal rules. The general idea is that you cannot copy an unusual law onto other cases. So the רבנן keep the rule of בשר בחלב limited to בשר בחלב only.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority opinion arguing with רבי עקיבא)
We learn / we derive
A unique, unusual law that does not follow normal logic, so other laws cannot be learned from it

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that you cannot learn from a חידוש is a basic tool used throughout ש״ס to block a derivation.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: Short question: why don't they learn from meat and milk too?

phrases.english: From meat in milk we do not derive,
because it is a novelty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing רבי עקיבא's source, the גמרא explains why the רבנן reject that source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the רבנן do not learn טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בשר בחלב is a חידוש, and we do not learn from a חידוש.

steps.title: What is the חידוש of בשר בחלב? A first suggestion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the חידוש is, and suggests: meat alone and milk alone are allowed, but together they are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the חידוש? If you say it is that this alone is allowed and that alone is allowed, but together they are forbidden...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exactly makes בשר בחלב a חידוש, and offers a first possible answer. This sets up the next move, where that answer will be rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that it is strange for two permitted foods to become forbidden just by being combined. The word אילימא signals that this answer is only being tested and will probably be pushed away.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will usually be rejected)
By itself / alone
Together with each other
Permitted

phrases.english: And what is the novelty?
If you say that this one by itself
and that one by itself are permitted,
and together they are forbidden,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the חידוש claimed in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is the unusual feature of בשר בחלב.

steps.title: כלאים works the same way, so that is not unusual
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected: כלאים also has two things that are allowed alone but forbidden together.
steps.simpleTranslation: כלאים too: this alone is allowed and that alone is allowed, but together they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion. כלאים also has the same pattern, so that pattern is not something unique to בשר בחלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חידוש must be something that appears nowhere else. With כלאים, each type of seed (or wool and linen) is fine alone, but mixing them is forbidden. Since this pattern shows up in another law, it is normal, not a חידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixtures of different kinds (like certain seeds together, or wool and linen)
Also / too
Forbidden

phrases.english: Diverse kinds too:
this by itself and that by itself are permitted,
and together they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested definition from step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the suggested definition of the חידוש, not the claim that בשר בחלב is a חידוש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'allowed alone, forbidden together' pattern also exists in כלאים, so it is not unique.

steps.title: The real novelty: soaking all day is allowed, but cooking is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The real חידוש: meat soaked in milk all day is allowed by Torah law, but meat cooked in milk even briefly is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the חידוש is that if one soaks it in milk all day, it is allowed; if he cooks it even a little, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real חידוש of בשר בחלב. Soaking meat in milk the whole day is allowed by Torah law, but cooking it in milk, even briefly, makes it forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if a forbidden taste goes into food, it doesn't matter how it got there. Here, a long soak surely puts milk taste into the meat, yet the Torah does not forbid it, while short cooking does. Only cooking makes it forbidden, and that is unlike any other law, so it is a true חידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (brings the correct answer after rejecting the first one)
Soaked
The whole day
Cooked
In milk

steps.confusionAlert: Soaking meat in milk is only allowed by Torah law. This does not mean it is allowed in practice. The point is just that the Torah's prohibition depends on cooking.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the Torah prohibition of בשר בחלב depends on cooking, not just on taste getting in. That is why the רבנן say it cannot be a source for טעם כעיקר in general.

phrases.english: Rather:
that if one soaks it the whole day
in milk, it is permitted,
if he cooked it with cooking, even briefly, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּאִי תָּרוּ לֵיהּ כּוּלֵּי יוֹמָא בַּחֲלָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected definition from steps 12-13 with the correct one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חידוש is that a long soak, which surely passes taste, is allowed, while cooking, even briefly, is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן don't learn טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב because it is a חידוש: soaking all day is allowed, but cooking is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא should also agree that בשר בחלב is a חידוש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי עקיבא must also agree that בשר בחלב is a חידוש, so how can he learn from it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא too, surely בשר בחלב is a חידוש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around on רבי עקיבא. If בשר בחלב is clearly a חידוש, how can רבי עקיבא learn טעם כעיקר from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning in step 14 seems true for everyone, not just the רבנן. So רבי עקיבא's source from step 10 now looks weak. The גמרא will have to explain how רבי עקיבא can still learn from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainly / surely
The תנא who holds that we learn טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva too,
is meat in milk not certainly a novelty?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא נָמֵי, בָּשָׂר בְּחָלָב וַדַּאי חִידּוּשׁ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the חידוש defined in step 14 to challenge רבי עקיבא's source from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's derivation of טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב (step 10).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If בשר בחלב is clearly a חידוש, and we never learn from a חידוש, then רבי עקיבא should not be able to learn טעם כעיקר from it either.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns from koshering non-Jewish pots
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא does not learn טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב. He learns it from גיעולי גוים: a non-Jew's pot holds only absorbed taste, yet the Torah forbids it. The same applies everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he learns it from the koshering of non-Jewish pots. When a non-Jew's pot needs koshering, isn't it only because of taste? And still it is forbidden. Here too, it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 15. רבי עקיבא's real source for טעם כעיקר is the koshering of non-Jewish pots, not בשר בחלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the war with מדין, the Torah required pots taken from non-Jews to be koshered before use. The pot contains no actual forbidden food, only absorbed taste, and still the Torah forbids it. That shows taste alone is enough to forbid food, which is exactly the rule of טעם כעיקר.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns / derives (a law from a source)
Koshering (purging) pots that non-Jews used for cooking
Mere taste, with no actual forbidden substance
It is no different; the same rule applies

phrases.english: Rather, he derives it from the purging of gentiles' vessels:

phrases.aramaic: גִּיעוּלֵי גוֹיִם, לָאו טַעְמָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא, וְאָסוּר?
phrases.english: Purging gentiles' vessels: isn't it only mere taste, and yet it is forbidden?
Here too, it is no different.
phrases.notes: "Here" means every other case of forbidden taste mixed into food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of Step 15 by replacing בשר בחלב with a different source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Substitution of source (אלא: switching to a different derivation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא learns טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב, which is a חידוש.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא learns טעם כעיקר from גיעולי גוים, where taste alone forbids.

steps.title: The רבנן say koshering non-Jewish pots is also a special exception
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reject this source too. Normally a taste that spoils the food (נותן טעם לפגם) is permitted, as we learn from נבילה. Yet a non-Jew's pot is forbidden, so גיעולי גוים is a חידוש and cannot teach a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? Koshering non-Jewish pots is also a special exception. Normally, anything that gives a bad, spoiling taste is permitted, as we learn from נבילה. But here it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן do not accept גיעולי גוים as a source. To them it is also a חידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule is that a forbidden taste that makes food worse does not forbid it. This is learned from נבילה: meat too spoiled to give even to a גר is not called נבילה at all. An old pot gives off a spoiled taste, yet the Torah still forbids it. Since this goes against the normal rule, it is a חידוש, and we cannot learn other laws from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives a taste that spoils or worsens the food (normally permitted)
Permitted
We learn (this rule from a source)
An animal that died without proper שחיטה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two "spoilings." The pot is not forbidden because its taste is good. The point is that the Torah forbids it even though its taste is bad, and that is exactly what makes it unusual.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן, גִּיעוּלֵי גוֹיִם נָמֵי חִידּוּשׁ הוּא.
phrases.english: And the Rabbis: purging gentiles' vessels is also a novelty.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא כׇּל נוֹתֵן טַעַם לִפְגָם — מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: For anything that gives a spoiling taste is permitted,
as we derive from an animal carcass,
phrases.notes: A carcass unfit even for a גר is not considered נבילה.

phrases.english: and here it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, גִּיעוּלֵי גוֹיִם נָמֵי חִידּוּשׁ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 16's new source with the same argument used against בשר בחלב in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's derivation of טעם כעיקר from גיעולי גוים (Step 16)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A law that breaks the normal rule (here, forbidding a spoiling taste) is a חידוש, and we cannot learn general principles from it.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: only a same-day pot was forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא follows רב חייא בריה דרב הונא, who says the Torah forbade only a pot used that same day. Such a pot gives a good taste, not a spoiling one, so גיעולי גוים is not a חידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא holds like רב חייא, son of רב הונא, who said: the Torah forbade only a pot that was used that same day. So it is not a case of a spoiling taste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי עקיבא answers the רבנן. He limits the Torah's prohibition to fresh, same-day pots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 24 hours pass, absorbed taste in a pot goes bad. רב חייא בריה דרב הונא holds the Torah only forbade a pot used within the day, while the taste is still good. A good taste forbidding food is normal and not a חידוש, so רבי עקיבא can learn טעם כעיקר from it.

keyTerms.meaning: A pot used within the last day (24 hours), whose absorbed taste is still fresh
The Torah did not forbid (except in this case)
Therefore

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that a pot older than a day (אינו בן יומו) gives a spoiling taste becomes a foundational principle in the laws of kashering and kitchen utensils.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא כִּדְרַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva holds like Rav Chiya, son of Rav Huna,
who said: The Torah did not forbid
except a pot used that same day,

phrases.aramaic: הִלְכָּךְ לָאו נוֹתֵן טַעַם לִפְגָם הוּא.
phrases.english: therefore it is not a case of giving a spoiling taste.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא כִּדְרַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends Step 16 against the challenge in Step 17 by narrowing the case of the Torah's prohibition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (limiting the law to a same-day pot)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: גיעולי גוים forbids even a spoiling taste, making it a חידוש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah forbade only a בת יומא pot, whose taste is not spoiling, so it is not a חידוש.

steps.title: The רבנן: even a same-day pot spoils the taste a little
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reply that even a pot used that same day must spoil the taste slightly. So גיעולי גוים still forbids a spoiling taste and stays a חידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? Even with a pot used that same day, it is impossible that it does not spoil the taste a little.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's answer to רבי עקיבא's defense. They reject the claim that a same-day pot gives a fully good taste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even granting that the Torah is speaking about a בת יומא pot, the רבנן say any taste absorbed into a pot's walls is at least slightly spoiled. So the Torah is still forbidding a spoiling taste, which goes against the rule from נבילה. Therefore גיעולי גוים remains a חידוש, and the רבנן do not learn טעם כעיקר from it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is impossible
It spoils / worsens (the taste)
A little, slightly

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא learns טעם כעיקר from גיעולי גוים, because a בת יומא pot gives a good taste, so it is not a חידוש. The רבנן hold that even a בת יומא pot spoils the taste slightly, so גיעולי גוים is a חידוש, just like בשר בחלב, and cannot teach טעם כעיקר.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: Asks how the רבנן respond to רבי עקיבא's defense.

phrases.english: Even a pot used that same day,
it is impossible that it does not spoil the taste a little.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense in Step 18 and reinstates the רבנן's claim from Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי עקיבא's claim that a בת יומא pot gives no spoiling taste.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes a same-day pot's taste is fully good. In fact, absorbed taste is always slightly spoiled, so the law is still a חידוש.

steps.title: If the רבנן generalize from the word מִשְׁרַת, רבי עקיבא should too
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא argues that רבי עקיבא should treat ״משרת״ the same way the רבנן do. The רבנן take ״משרת״ to teach טעם כעיקר and extend it to the whole Torah. So רבי עקיבא's lesson from ״משרת״, היתר מצטרף לאיסור, should also extend to the whole Torah. This goes against רבי יוחנן, who limits it to נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רב אויא, said to רב אשי: Let us learn how רבי עקיבא thinks from how the רבנן think. Don't the רבנן say that the word 'soaked' (משרת) teaches that taste counts like the actual food, and from here you apply it to all prohibitions in the Torah? So for רבי עקיבא too: the word 'soaked' teaches that permitted food joins with forbidden food, and from here you should apply it to all prohibitions in the whole Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge opens. רב אחא says that both sides learn something from the same word ״משרת״. Since the רבנן apply their lesson to every prohibition, רבי עקיבא should apply his lesson to every prohibition too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is a parallel. Both sides read the same verse about a נזיר. If one reading is spread to the whole Torah, the other reading should be spread the same way. If that is true, then היתר מצטרף לאיסור applies to every prohibition, which contradicts רבי יוחנן's statement that it applies only to נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Soaking' – the word in the נזיר verse (grape soakings) that both sides learn from
Permitted food joins with forbidden food to make up the minimum amount for a punishment
'From here you derive' – this one case serves as a model for all similar cases
'Let us learn' – here it means: let us figure out one opinion by comparing it to another
An אמורא who raises this challenge to רב אשי

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two lessons from ״משרת״. The רבנן learn טעם כעיקר from it, meaning taste alone counts as the food. רבי עקיבא learns היתר מצטרף לאיסור from it, meaning permitted food helps fill up the כזית (olive-sized minimum). These are two different rules drawn from the same word.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this challenge succeeds, היתר מצטרף לאיסור would apply to every prohibition. That would mean a person could be punished for eating a mixture even when the forbidden part alone is less than a כזית.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Avya, said to Rav Ashi:
From the Rabbis, let us learn about Rabbi Akiva,
phrases.notes: He compares how the two sides use the same word.

phrases.english: don't the Rabbis say
that 'soaked' comes to make taste like the substance,

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן אַתָּה דָּן לְכׇל אִיסּוּרִין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: and from here you derive it for all prohibitions in the Torah?
For Rabbi Akiva as well —
'soaked' teaches that the permitted joins with the forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן אַתָּה דָּן לְכׇל אִיסּוּרִין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ!
phrases.english: so from here you should derive it for all prohibitions in the entire Torah!
phrases.notes: This conclusion contradicts רבי יוחנן, who limits the rule to נזיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּרַבָּנַן נִשְׁמַע לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, מִי לָא אָמְרִי רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the debate over the source of טעם כעיקר (steps 15–19). The גמרא now asks how far היתר מצטרף לאיסור reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's position that היתר מצטרף לאיסור applies only to נזיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sides draw from the same word ״משרת״. The רבנן spread their lesson to all prohibitions, so רבי עקיבא's lesson should spread to all prohibitions as well. That makes רבי יוחנן's limit to נזיר hard to accept.

steps.title: רב אשי begins his reply
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי starts to answer רב אחא. Only the opening words appear on this amud, and the answer itself continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is opening רב אשי's answer, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No content has been given yet, only the speaker. The reply will explain why רבי עקיבא's lesson from ״משרת״ does not spread to the whole Torah, even though the רבנן's lesson does.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He said to him' – the formula that opens a reply
A leading אמורא who answers the challenge

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב אשי's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the reply to רב אחא's challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pending – the reply continues on the next amud
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's היתר מצטרף לאיסור should apply to the whole Torah, just as the רבנן's טעם כעיקר does.
steps.terutzMaskana: To be stated on the next amud.
